newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JULY 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JULY 4.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Under pressure from within ruling party PASOK and from the need for structural change in the Greek economy, Prime Minister Costas Simitis again sought answers in the centre-left, stressing in his speech last night that the dilemma of the 21st century was choosing between "socialism controlled by people for the people's development or social anarchy with growth under conditions of extreme individualism and cultural barbarism." He attacked the "rule of the law of profits which places a price on everything" and creating an "unstable international environment with the only stable element... profit margins".

--Simitis will endeavour to promote the inclusion of Balkan states in NATO at the Madrid summit next week despite the US making it clear that the first phase of expansion will include only Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary. Simitis will have support from France and other European states and will attempt to get a commitment from NATO for an "open door" policy for former Communist states.

--Unionists are unimpressed by the 20-point proposal from employers for changes to the job market, responding positively to just one proposal, considering another and rejecting the rest. Unionists responded with their own list: ploughing profits back into industry, a 35-hour working week, and "increased full-time jobs rather than shared poverty".

--Spurned lover Thanassis Koutsoyiannakis yesterday gunned down his former sister-in-law before turning the gun on himself, after learning she was to marry. The double murder-suicide was the ninth incident in which women have been violently killed by their partners or former partners since 1993.

--One card will open the doors of all Greece's banks and looks set to revolutionise the way Greeks bank. The card will be extended to Greece's 366,000 pensioners, putting an end to endless queues at banks and public offices and will also be distributed to all civil servants to access their pay, which will be paid directly into accounts.

--Main opposition New Democracy party will bring claims by a consortium bidding for the Thessaloniki Metro project that the tender has been undermined by the environment, town planning and public works ministry to Parliament.
--Three major hopsitals will be out of action over the next few days, as the temperatures climb to expected highs of 40 degrees Celsius.

--A draft bill from the interior ministry foresees changes in the elections of mayors, prefects and other officials and subsequent redistribution of responsibilities. The changes will be in place for the next round of municipal elections in October 1998. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
